q: you would say that ocerall my moves I have made suggested by the system have actually hurt me more than helped me? That kind of sucks. I wonder though on a game by game basis like (espn fantasy games), if it actually helped me, not jsut total net points?
short: On the season ledger your roster moves are net -456 points, but game by game they were roughly +60 in your Week 1 loss and -60 in your Week 2 win, so neither result changed. I can't separate system-suggested moves from your own.
answer:
Short version: by the season ledger in your dashboard, your 10 adds and 8 drops are net -456 points, so on raw totals they cost you. That number is harsher than the real effect, though, and matchup by matchup the moves did not change who won either completed week.

One limit up front: the data does not record which moves came from the system's suggestions and which you made on your own. So I can only grade all of your roster moves together.

Where the -456 comes from: the ledger compares what each added player scored for you against everything the dropped player has scored anywhere since. The big negatives are dropping Julian Champagnie (198 points since) for Bobby Portis (20), then dropping Portis for Scotty Pippen Jr. (Portis scored 164 after you cut him, Pippen 45), dropping Precious Achiuwa (201) for Aaron Gordon (74), and dropping Day'Ron Sharpe (117) for Alex Sarr (35). The best were Payton Pritchard (+100, a pure add), Andrew Wiggins (+36) and the P.J. Washington add on 10-20 (127 points for you vs 169 from Camara). The flaw in this method is that it counts every point a dropped player scores, including on other teams' benches, and ignores whether he would have fit in your lineup. So it overstates the damage. Still, the early drops of Champagnie, Achiuwa and Sharpe look like real misses. For context, Garebears sit at -456, similar to teams 8 (-490) and 1 (-546), while teams 4, 5 and 7 are positive.

Game by game (your actual ESPN matchups), using lineup points only, as a rough estimate:

Week 1, a loss 1249 to 1288 (39 points). The week 1 adds (Washington 84, Pippen 26, Portis 20) scored about 130 in your lineup, against about 59 from the players you dropped, so the moves were roughly +50 to +70. Without them you would have lost by more. They did not flip it.

Week 2, a win 1370 to 1135 (235 points). The adds scored about 212 in your lineup, while Camara, Champagnie, Sharpe and Achiuwa put up about 245 elsewhere that week, so the moves were roughly 40 to 80 points worse. You would have won anyway.

Week 3 is live and you trail Team 9 715 to 896 with days left. So far the moves are about neutral: Wiggins has 35 and Sarr 33 in your lineup, while the players you dropped (Pippen, Poeltl) have produced 0 elsewhere this week. Zubac has not scored for you yet.

Honest read: in the two finished weeks the moves were roughly +60 and -60, a wash, and neither result would have changed. The season total looks bad mostly because of a few drops of useful players in the first two weeks. For future moves, check how much a dropped player is likely to keep producing, not just whether the add projects slightly higher, and drop bench players first. My weekly splits come from the daily lineup history and are approximate, since a claim's processing day can shift a few games between weeks. I did not search the web, since this is about your own logs.

moves.do: Before your next drop, compare the dropped player's per game average with the add's, and cut bench players first
moves.why: Champagnie (198 pts), Achiuwa (201) and Sharpe (117) scored far more after being cut than the players who replaced them (20, 74, 35).
